text:
maria.g: Heads up — RT dashboard p99 for usage_rollups spiked ~3x at 04:12 UTC. Looks correlated with the retention-rollup job reindexing. Seeing node CPU and Kafka consumer lag increases.

siva: saw it. Consumer 'usage-rollup-aggregator' jumped lag to ~40k at the same time. I'm replicating locally with a smaller dataset.

jamie: quick note: the p99 panel still points to raw_events and computes aggregates client-side (hourly scans). That was meant to be temporary.

tyler: we have a preagg table (usage_rollup_preagg) we deployed in staging last month — dashboard wasn't switched over. Can we flip to that to stop the full scans?

maria.g: yes, good call. Another factor: retention job triggered a full reprocess/compaction after backfill. I think compaction IO throttled the k8s nodes and added CPU pressure which slowed consumers.

nora: logs from the job (tail):
```
2026-03-18T04:10:58Z INFO retention-rollup: starting window 2026-03-18T00:00Z -> 2026-03-18T04:00Z
2026-03-18T04:11:12Z WARN retention-rollup: compaction job started (reason=backfill)
2026-03-18T04:12:05Z ERROR k8s-node-3: kubelet CPU 95%
2026-03-18T04:12:20Z ERROR kafka-consumer usage-rollup-aggregator: lag=40234
```

ops-bot: Alert triggered: rollup-job-high-latency at 1806257940 (severity=warning)

jamie: suggested immediate mitigations:
- switch p99 and p95 panels to usage_rollup_preagg
- add short-term sampling for p99 queries (e.g. sample 1/10) until preagg is validated
- throttle compaction job IO (set io.limit on the job)

siva: I can patch the consumer to use topic-level backpressure config and bump `max.poll.interval.ms` temporarily. Will also add a retry/backoff to avoid compaction overlap.

tyler: I'll update the dashboard JSON now. SQL for panel change: 
```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', ts) as ts, approx_percentile(p99_latency, 0.99) as p99_latency
FROM usage_rollup_preagg
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
```

maria.g: plan and owners: 
- siva: patch aggregator consumer + add backoff (ETA 1h)
- jamie: update dashboard to preagg + add sampling fallback (ETA 30m)
- tyler: throttle compaction job IO and add cron jitter (ETA 45m)
- nora: validate node health and move any critical pods off stressed nodes (ongoing)

nora: quick health snapshot after initial fixes: nodes recovered to 40-60% CPU within 12 minutes after throttling compaction. Consumer lag dropping.

siva: pushed consumer patch to canary -> set `max.poll.interval.ms=300000` and `fetch.max.bytes` reduced. Consumer lag down to ~1.2k.

jamie: dashboard switched to preagg and sample fallback in place. Panels now render <500ms for p99. Saved dashboard version `usage/rt-p99-preagg-20260318`.

maria.g: ops summary for postmortem: root cause = overlapping heavy compaction + dashboard full scans; contributing = no preagg usage on RT panels + compaction without IO limits. ACTIONS:
- enforce preagg for all high-cardinality RT panels (jamie)
- add compaction IO defaults and require IO limit flags on backfills (tyler)
- add a metric `gpu_alloc_delta` to preagg schema to help capacity forecasting for GPU-backed workloads (siva)
- add a short-term alert for 'dashboard-query-scan-rate' when panels scan >10M rows in 5m (maria.g)

tyler: I'll schedule a controlled re-run of the backfill with IO caps and a canary to monitor consumer lag. Target maintenance window 08:00 UTC.

maria.g: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a tiny postmortem doc (1-paragraph + action list) and update the forecasting pipeline to ingest `usage_rollup_preagg` counts instead of raw events for capacity headroom models.

ops-bot: Incident resolved ticket #INF-2026-198 closed by maria.g at 1806261200
